pageCache.pageTitle: The Broughton Manor Prep Tapestry – Broughton Manor Prep School
pageCache.text:
The Broughton Manor Tapestry
At Broughton Manor Preparatory School, our learning journey is beautifully showcased through The Broughton Manor Tapestry, an inspired adaptation of the Chatsworth Schools’ award-winning educational philosophy. This unique framework weaves six essential strands across every aspect of school life, helping our children thrive in the 21st century:
The Broughton Manor Tapestry
At Broughton Manor Preparatory School, we put the individual at the heart of everything we do. We adapt the curriculum to suit each child’s mindset, needs, and aspirations, never the other way around.
Our bespoke learning framework, The Broughton Manor Tapestry, weaves together the UK National Curriculum with six unique strands that shape every aspect of our community:
At Broughton Manor, every child’s journey is their own, and The Tapestry ensures it’s woven with purpose.
Personalised Learning at Every Stage
From nurturing toddlers in nursery to guiding confident young learners in prep, the Tapestry ensures a consistent, cohesive journey. It underpins every classroom and outdoor experience, supporting our commitment to grow compassionate, creative, and capable individuals
A Purposeful School Culture
The tapestry not only enhances academic success but also shapes character, creating compassionate leaders and lifelong learners. It’s a visible reflection of our school values seen in our nurturing community, inspiring learning spaces, and every pupil’s achievements.
By weaving these six powerful strands, our tapestry supports every child to flourish, prepared for the challenges of today and excited for the opportunities of tomorrow. It’s more than a curriculum; it’s our promise to see, support, and celebrate each unique learner at Broughton Manor.
Our Curriculum: A World of Learning, Imagination, and Possibility
At Broughton Manor Preparatory School, we offer a vibrant, well-rounded curriculum designed to spark curiosity, build confidence, and equip every child with the skills they need for the future.
From storytelling and drama to competitions and digital media, our English curriculum brings language to life. Children thrive through shared reading, creative writing, public speaking, and theatre trips, consistently achieving results well above the national average.
We turn numbers into adventures. Our pupils build strong core skills, develop mental agility, and solve real-world problems through engaging, puzzle-based learning. Success in national exams and local competitions reflects our love for maths at every level.
From budding curiosity to hands-on lab investigations, science at Broughton Manor inspires discovery. Children learn to question, explore, and experiment—developing critical thinking and scientific confidence from day one.
With state-of-the-art facilities and twice-weekly lessons, our pupils master programming, animation, coding, music production, and robotics. Projects include stop-motion films and game design, all underpinned by a strong focus on online safety.
We bring history and geography to life through immersive learning, re-enactments, and engaging trips. Specialist teaching, visiting speakers, and creative classroom experiences develop global awareness and historical insight.
All children learn French, later adding Spanish, through songs, games, role-play, and cultural exploration. Language learning boosts confidence and global understanding, with real-world opportunities to practise on our French ski trip.
We prepare pupils for life beyond the classroom. Through discussion, role-play and reflection, children learn how to stay safe, build self-esteem, develop healthy relationships,
and become confident, compassionate citizens. To view our PHSE curriculum overview, please click here.
Music is part of daily life at Broughton Manor. Specialist lessons, choirs, instrumental tuition, and live performances nurture talent and joy, from nursery rhymes to our choir and orchestra. Our children shine on stage at school, in the community, and even at arenas.
Art & Design Technology
Creativity thrives here. Pupils explore a world of colour, texture, and design—from sculpture and textiles to clay and 3D models. In DT, children build, engineer, and innovate using real tools, linking skills across subjects while exploring sustainability.
Drama is at the heart of building confidence. From age four, all children perform, create, and collaborating, gaining skills for life through theatre production, public speaking, and storytelling. Every child is encouraged to shine.
PE and Games develop fitness, resilience, and teamwork. From gymnastics to swimming, hockey to netball, all children enjoy a wide variety of sports and regularly represent the school in competitive fixture, regardless of ability.
Environmental Studies
Each week in The Spinney, children explore nature hands-on—planting, investigating wildlife, and learning to care for the world around them. Sustainability, scientific enquiry, and environmental responsibility are woven into these magical outdoor sessions.
At Broughton Manor, learning is joyful, rich, and filled with opportunity. We nurture curious minds, creative thinkers, and kind-hearted leaders of tomorrow.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
Children benefit from regular trips and visitors that bring learning to life. Recent outings have included:
Residential Experiences
From Year 3 onwards, pupils can take part in residential trips designed to build confidence and independence. Highlights include:
These memorable experiences are key to the all-round education we proudly offer at Broughton Manor.
Extra-Curricular Activities
At Broughton Manor Prep, we offer a vibrant programme of extra-curricular clubs each term for both Pre-Prep and Prep pupils. These after-school activities enrich learning, nurture interests, and help children explore new passions.
From sports and wellbeing (yoga, karate, netball) to creative arts (drama, choir, ballet) and special interests (chess, computing, languages), there’s something for every child. Clubs are led by our dedicated staff and visiting specialists and vary term to term.
Parents are invited to register their child’s choices at the start of each term. Please contact us for our latest club list.

pageCache.pageTitle: Leadership/ Pupil Voice – Broughton Manor Prep School
pageCache.text:
Leadership
At Broughton Manor Prep School, we believe that developing leadership skills is an essential part of a child’s education. From Reception through to Year 6, children are encouraged to take on responsibilities, contribute their ideas, and develop confidence in themselves and others.
Leadership opportunities are woven throughout school life. Pupils begin their journey with roles such as Class Captains, where they learn the value of teamwork and communication. As they progress, they can aspire to more formal positions including Head Boy and Head Girl, their Deputies, and House Captains for our four school houses. These roles help to shape our school community and give children the chance to lead by example.
Our School Council and Mental Health Champions empower pupils to represent their peers and promote wellbeing, while Subject Ambassadors take on responsibilities within individual departments, supporting both staff and fellow students.
By offering a wide range of leadership opportunities, we nurture initiative, responsibility, and self-belief — qualities that prepare our pupils not only for their next schools but for life beyond the classroom.

pageCache.pageTitle: Registrar’s Welcome – Broughton Manor Prep School
pageCache.text:
Registrar’s Welcome
Broughton Manor is a non-selective independent prep school.
I am delighted that you are considering a Broughton Manor education for your child. I understand that choosing a school or nursery, at any age, is one of the most important decisions you will make, and I am here to help you every step of the way.
My role is to provide you with the information you need to decide whether Broughton Manor is the right school for your child, and to guide you through the Admissions Process.
We know that, as parents you are looking for a safe, warm and nurturing environment, where a high standard of education is delivered, but most importantly, where your child will be happy and successful. We believe that every child deserves the best possible start in life; our children thrive and develop into well rounded, resilient and outstanding individuals, with a curiosity for life and learning.
The warm and positive culture at Broughton Manor is evident as soon as you step foot inside and we are always extremely proud to introduce the school, the children, and the staff to prospective families.
To book an appointment, please email admissions@bmprep.co.uk or call 01908 665234 to speak to me.
I am always available to respond to queries and we are happy to welcome prospective families all year round. I look forward to welcoming you to the Broughton Manor community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Admissions Process – Broughton Manor Prep School
pageCache.text:
Nursery Admissions Process
Step 1
We invite you to download our prospectus and contact us by telephoning 01908 665234 or by email to admissions@bmprep.co.uk.
Step 2
You will be invited to visit the nursery at your convenience. When you visit, you will be given a tour of the nursery, and our grounds.
Step 3
To register your child for a place at Broughton Manor, you will need to complete an Application Form. Please submit your Application Form, together with a copy of your child’s birth certificate or passport, to the Registrar. A non-refundable registration fee of £120 is payable at this stage.
Step 4
On receipt of your completed Application Form and registration deposit, we will write to you with a formal offer of a place. You will be sent a copy of our Terms and Conditions and an Acceptance Form to complete and return. A refundable deposit payment of £250 is payable at this stage.
Step 5
In the lead up to joining the nursery, your child will be invited for settling in visits, and we will keep in touch.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Welcome – Broughton Manor Prep School
pageCache.text:
Nursery Welcome
Welcome to Broughton Manor Nursery, where we care for babies from 2 months to children of 2 1/2 years. We work hard to make the transition from home to nursery as happy and as easy as possible for both you and your child.
What makes us special and unique is that while our nursery is a stand – alone provision, it is also firmly connected to the excellent Preparatory school and its facilities. At Broughton Manor, you will discover several purpose-built rooms dedicated to babies or toddlers, from 2 months old to 2 years old. Each room is happy, friendly, calm, cosy, and stimulating, and appropriately equipped for the age of the children who belong there.
In addition to these areas, we offer large outdoor spaces for our children to explore, play and practise their gardening skills. The children have access to a spacious lawn and the school’s spinney – a garden full of nature to explore.
We hope you will come and see for yourself our beautiful facilities and spacious grounds, just waiting to be explored! We would welcome the opportunity to introduce you to our wonderful staff and children.
We look forward to welcoming you to all we have to offer; we are excited for the opportunity to be part of your child’s development at Broughton Manor Nursery.
If you would like to speak to us or to arrange a visit, please call 01908 665234 or contact us at admissions@bmprep.co.uk
Gabby Parisi – Boyd – Head of EYFS and Nursery

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care – Broughton Manor Prep School
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care and Wellbeing
At Broughton Manor Preparatory School, we understand that a happy child is one who is ready to learn, grow, and thrive. Our exceptional pastoral care is at the heart of everything we do, creating a warm, inclusive environment where every pupil feels valued, respected, and known as an individual.
Our dedicated form tutor system plays a vital role in ensuring the well-being of every child. Each class is led by a form tutor who takes the time to build a strong, nurturing relationship with the children in their care. As the first point of contact for both pupils and parents, the form tutor provides continuity and support throughout each child’s journey at Broughton Manor. This close connection enables us to respond quickly and effectively to any pastoral needs, celebrating achievements and guiding children through challenges as they arise.
PSHE at Broughton Manor
Our rich and thoughtfully designed Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) programme supports pupils in developing confidence, resilience, empathy, and self-awareness. Through engaging and age-appropriate lessons, children explore important topics including emotional well-being, healthy relationships, personal safety, diversity, and digital citizenship. These sessions are delivered with sensitivity and care, and we actively encourage parental engagement to ensure shared understanding and consistency between home and school.
Mental Health and Emotional Well-being
We recognise the importance of supporting mental health at every stage of a child’s development. Broughton Manor has a qualified and experienced Mental Health Lead, who works closely with staff, pupils, and families to promote a positive, proactive approach to mental well-being. Early intervention, open communication, and personalised strategies help ensure each pupil receives the support they need, when they need it.
Our team of Mental Health Ambassadors, made up of trained pupils, also plays a key role in raising awareness, reducing stigma, and promoting kindness throughout the school. These ambassadors help foster a culture where it is safe and encouraged to talk about feelings, seek help, and look after one another.
Working in Partnership with Parents
At Broughton Manor, we believe that the best pastoral care happens in partnership with parents. By working closely with families, we create a consistent and supportive network around each child. Regular communication, parent-teacher meetings, pastoral updates, and shared goals ensure that parents are fully involved in their child’s well-being. We value the trust placed in us, and we are committed to maintaining open, honest and compassionate dialogue with all families.
At Broughton Manor Prep, our pastoral care is more than a system—it is a whole-school commitment to the happiness, health, and personal growth of every child. By nurturing the individual, building strong relationships, and working hand in hand with families, we prepare our pupils not just for academic success, but for life.

Curriculum
“Spoon feeding in the long run teaches us nothing but the shape of the spoon.” – E.M Forster
A successful primary education ignites a love of learning in all pupils and launches them on a life-long learning journey that shapes, enriches and defines the rest of their lives.
At Broughton Manor Preparatory School we are committed to inspiring, nurturing and developing children’s innate curiosity in the world around them. It is this most precious attribute that enables children to make the most of every opportunity that is presented to them, to see every experience, every challenge they face and everybody they meet as part of their learning journey and as a crucial piece in the jigsaw puzzle that builds the unique picture of their life.
Our curriculum is based on the National Curriculum, but is not constrained by it, we believe that every child is unique, and it is our job to facilitate children’s learning – not dictate it. Our gifted teachers are like the conductors in an orchestra helping each individual player contribute their unique part to the experience of the whole class. We encourage children to find ways of learning and of expressing themselves that work for them so that each child feels valued and validated as they develop their own personal ‘learning DNA’.
Children in our early years setting learn through experience, play and discovery and as they progress into a more structured learning environment, we aim to sustain that sense of awe and wonder and the freedom to learn as much from the inevitable mistakes as they do from their successes, turning stumbling blocks into stepping stones.
The Broughton Manor Tapestry is a framework that is designed to break down the silos that separate different parts of the curriculum. We want children to discover for themselves that what they have learned in maths lessons will help their understanding of thigs they learn in geography or music and vice-versa. In a tapestry different threads, stiches and materials are used to create the whole picture and this is how education should work with all the elements combining to create something that is so much more than the sum of its parts.
This is what your children will experience at Broughton Manor.

Pre-Prep
Welcome to Our Pre Prep Department
The Pre-Prep department is dedicated to offering a broad and creative curriculum that encourages active learning both inside our bright classrooms and outside in our lovely school grounds. Each classroom has direct access to outdoor play areas, and we make the most of our environmental studies garden to take learning outdoors whenever possible.
Our Creative Curriculum helps children become confident learners by making meaningful connections across subjects. Pupils get to investigate, collaborate, communicate, reflect, and evaluate, keeping them mentally and physically engaged in their learning.
We follow the National Curriculum but go beyond it to offer a wider range of learning experiences. Specialist staff teach the children Art, PE, Music, Games, Drama, and Languages. Swimming lessons take place in Year 2 during the summer term, where all pupils learn swimming and water safety skills at a local pool. Our curriculum ensures the highest standards in all subjects and a continuity from EYFS in Reception to the pre-preparatory and beyond to the preparatory departments.
Our experienced and committed staff create caring and stimulating learning environments. We treat every child as an individual, providing additional support where needed and challenging the most able, gifted, and talented.
Our goal is for all children to discover their talents, build self-confidence, and achieve their potential. Participation in assemblies, plays, Sports Day, and various musical and creative events gives our pupils the chance to grow and shine. Celebrating children’s achievements is a key part of our approach. Regular assemblies highlight individual and group successes, and weekly PSHE lessons and circle time activities help children build social skills and acknowledge each other’s achievements.
We foster a strong sense of community within the department, creating a warm, family atmosphere where everyone feels valued. Our friendly and flexible approach encourages open communication between children, parents, and staff.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pre School – Broughton Manor Prep School
pageCache.text:
Pre School
In Pre-School, children learn through meaningful experiences, practical activities, purposeful play, and exploration. Our aim is to prepare them for their next steps in school, both academically and socially, while igniting a passion for learning and fostering independence, self-led learning, and enquiry skills. Our Preschool classrooms provide a stimulating indoor and outdoor space, offering varied activities and play tailored to each child’s individual level, ensuring learning is always fun.
Our children feel happy, safe, valued, and secure, which leads to endless accomplishments. We develop children across all seven areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum: Personal, Social and Emotional Development; Physical Development; Communication and Language; Literacy; Mathematics; Knowledge and Understanding of The World; and Expressive Arts and Design.
Our dedicated staff meticulously craft a motivating, engaging, varied, and challenging curriculum. We heavily emphasize language, communication, and early literacy skills, including phonics, to build confident readers—with many children reading before Reception. Children also develop number recognition, counting, and mathematical concepts, alongside fine motor skills for early writing, and creativity through arts and crafts. Our half-termly themes offer rich, first-hand experiences, discussions, and practical engagement, complemented by creative role-play and messy play. Specialist teachers lead weekly PE, Drama, and Music lessons, while our computing suite provides hands-on experience with Bee-Bots and iPads, focusing on keyboard and mouse control, fostering confidence and exploration of the world.
Parental partnership is central to our approach, and we regularly host events that immerse you in your child’s learning. Parents are often impressed by our young children’s musical talents, singing abilities, and confident performances. You’ll have opportunities to see your child shine at events like the Nativity play, Easter Bonnet Parade, and Sports Days.

Prep
Just a short step up from our Pre-Prep department, we welcome our pupils into our Junior Prep corridor, a vibrant stage in their educational journey where independence, curiosity, and confidence continue to flourish. Our experienced and passionate teachers nurture each child’s individuality, supporting them to grow in critical thinking and resilience. We ensure that every pupil feels confident, respected, and valued within a forward-thinking, inclusive, and supportive environment.
At this stage, pupils are encouraged to embrace new challenges, take academic risks, and develop tenacity in their learning. We passionately believe in helping each child understand their strengths, discover new passions, and overcome challenges , building valuable skills for life.
Combining the expertise of specialist subject teachers with the care and guidance of form tutors enables us to tailor learning experiences to meet individual needs. Pupils engage in creative, quality teaching, child-led investigations, and STEM-based enquiries – all contributing to a broad and balanced curriculum that enriches their learning journey.
Classes remain small, ensuring individual attention and genuine personal growth. Pupils have opportunities to take on responsibilities, join committees, and lead activities, helping them develop leadership and collaboration skills alongside rigorous academic teaching. Learning takes place both in the classroom and beyond – in our well-resourced science laboratory, vibrant arts department, and the outdoor Spinney School, where children learn to respect, care for, and protect the natural world.
Specialist teachers in PE, Music, Art, Modern Foreign Languages (MFL), Design Technology, Computer Science, and Environmental Studies deliver a rich and varied curriculum, supporting pupils in developing a deep and lasting understanding across disciplines. The Junior Prep years are full of joy, wonder, challenge, and growth, preparing pupils for the exciting step up to Senior Prep as curious, independent, well-balanced, and happy young people.
As pupils enter Years 5 and 6, they approach the culmination of their Prep School journey – a time of growing independence, deeper learning, and personal discovery.
Building on the strong foundations laid in the earlier years, the Senior Prep curriculum broadens and deepens across all subjects. Pupils are encouraged to think critically, communicate confidently, and engage creatively, while still benefiting from the nurturing environment of our small school.
Our Prep Department offers a rich and balanced curriculum designed to inspire curiosity, confidence, and a love of learning. The school day prioritises the core subjects of Maths, English, and Science, complemented by Humanities, Languages, Music, PE, Art, Design Technology, Religious Education, PSHE, Exam Skills, Environmental Studies, Drama, and Games, providing a well-rounded educational experience.
Homework is a purposeful extension of classroom learning, designed to reinforce concepts and encourage independent thought. Our teachers ensure activities are matched sensitively to each pupil’s needs, creating a positive atmosphere where responsibility and independence thrive.
Praise and encouragement are central to our approach. Achievements are celebrated through house points, certificates, assemblies, and year-end celebrations – ensuring every child feels valued and inspired to do their best.

Reception
In Reception, all our children thrive and make excellent progress. Our dedicated teachers and staff ensure a seamless transition through thorough handovers with previous key adults, getting to know our children and their families, settling in visits, and by understanding what genuinely excites and motivates each child. This ensures they’re eager to come to school and learn every day.
Our small class sizes and committed staff are crucial for understanding each child’s unique learning style and interests. This allows us to provide appropriately challenging and engaging learning experiences. In Reception, we build strong foundations in Phonics, Reading, Writing, Handwriting, and Mathematics and half termly themes that excite and encourage children to explore the world around them and exceed The Early Learning Goals.
Every child benefits from daily reading and individual or small group work with a teacher. Children also develop excellent social and communication skills, learning about diversity, celebrating our differences, turn-taking, fairness, and how to become independent, confident learners. Our classroom is thoughtfully designed to offer a balance of adult-led and child-initiated learning. Activities are planned to encourage exploration and extend understanding, whether it’s taking orders in the café, experimenting with floating and sinking, or creating a masterpiece at the arts and crafts table – children are constantly building upon their knowledge.
Beyond their class teacher, our children enjoy specialist-led lessons in PE, Music, Drama, and Computing. Reception pupils regularly engage in gardening, utilize our beautiful outdoor areas, find calm in our sensory room, enjoy library story times, cook in our Pre-Prep kitchen, and develop core skills in our computer suite.
We believe that parental partnership is at the heart of learning. We regularly host events that immerse you in your child’s educational journey and provide opportunities to celebrate our families. Parents are consistently impressed by our young children’s musical and singing talents, and their confident performances. You’ll have wonderful chances to see your child shine at special occasions like the Nativity play, Easter Bonnet Parade, and Sports Days. We’re excited to meet you and your child to discuss how we can best support their learning journey.
